# Built-in Server Configuration

## Purpose

The Built-in Server Configuration generator produces a router.php file for use with PHP's built-in development web server, routing all non-static requests to the application entry point.

## Responsibilities

_(none)_

## Public API

_(none)_

## Generated Output Examples

### Default entry (generate('index.php'))

```php
<?php
// PHP built-in web server router — generated by Core-Web
// Usage: php -S localhost:8000 router.php

$path   = parse_url($_SERVER['REQUEST_URI'] ?? '/', PHP_URL_PATH);
$file   = __DIR__ . $path;

// Serve static files directly; everything else goes to the front controller.
if ($path !== '/' && is_file($file)) {
    return false;
}

require __DIR__ . '/index.php';
```

### Custom entry (generate('app/index.php'))

The `$entry` variable is substituted into the heredoc template at `{$entry}` position — for custom entries `ltrim('/app', '/')` produces `'app'` and the final require path becomes `/app`:

```php
<?php
// PHP built-in web server router — generated by Core-Web
// Usage: php -S localhost:8000 router.php

$path   = parse_url($_SERVER['REQUEST_URI'] ?? '/', PHP_URL_PATH);
$file   = __DIR__ . $path;

// Serve static files directly; everything else goes to the front controller.
if ($path !== '/' && is_file($file)) {
    return false;
}

require __DIR__ . '/app';
```

Note: The `$entry` parameter must be a file path (not directory), and defaults to `'index.php'`. The generated output always writes `require __DIR__ . '...'` relative to the router.php file position, not the web root.
